Q: Why two NaNs with the same binary are still not equal to each other but two infs are? A:

Nans and infs are not numbers, mathematical operations are not defined for them.

Yes they are.

Specifically in this case they are floating-point numbers, and all floating-point mathematical operations are fully defined for them. In the context of programming, it is most likely the IEEE 754 standard doing the defining.

The mathematical operation of equality is explicitly defined for all these cases. The binary representation of any type is just an implementation detail, and not relevant to its defined behaviour.

  • 0.0 == -0.0 -> True
  • inf == inf -> True
  • inf == -inf -> False
  • NaN == Nan -> False
  • NaN == inf -> False

The numbers you use in computers (IEEE 754 floating-point, fixed-width integers, etc.) are not the same as the numbers you use in pure mathematics (naturals, rationals, reals). They have different definitions and different behaviour.

Does C check whether any of the two number is NaN before doing any comparison every time?

C doesn't check anything. It's a language not an implementation. Any conforming implementation (usually hardware) that handles floating-point operations must ensure the defined results are produced.

Sometimes there is a "fast fp" option that will skip things like renormalisation and NaN checks in order to execute faster, but at the cost of sometimes returning the wrong answer. In practice I think it's more likely to result in something becoming NaN when it shouldn't, rather than a NaN overflowing to some other value.

Q: Creating or using a telegram bot that forward messages received from a bot to another account A:

Install Telethon

python3 -m pip install --upgrade pip
python3 -m pip install --upgrade telethon

Obtain your API_ID and API_TOKEN from Telegram

And then replace your values and run the code:

from telethon import TelegramClient, events
import asyncio
import logging
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.WARNING)

api_id = # don't forget to fill this 
api_hash = '' # don't forget to fill this 

client = TelegramClient("forwarder", api_id, api_hash)
client.start()


from_chat_id = # don't forget to fill this
to_chat_id = "me"


async def get_chat_id(title):
    async for dialog in client.iter_dialogs():        
        if dialog.title == title:        
            return dialog.id


@client.on(events.NewMessage)
async def my_event_handler(event):
    chat = await event.get_chat()
    if chat.id == from_chat_id:
        await client.forward_messages(to_chat_id, event.message)

# asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete(get_chat_id("YOUR CHAT TITLE"))
asyncio.get_event_loop().run_forever()

from_chat_id will be the chat id of the bot you want to forward message from.

to_chat_id will be the destination chat id. using 'me' would forward the message to your saved messages.

Another thing to note is this code:

asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete(get_chat_id("YOUR CHAT TITLE"))

if you want to get the id of a chat you can uncomment this line and pass your chat title.
